A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ScaleGUN and contain the complete main text and Appendices A–E. Their text, equations, algorithms, tables, figures, and proofs support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original accuracy, runtime, unlearning-efficacy, and parameter-study results on six graph datasets.

after.justification: The original empirical evaluations remain, with revised utility results and an additional comparative gradient-residual analysis in Appendix C.4.

M1.justification: The lazy local propagation, approximate Newton update, perturbed objective, and budget-triggered retraining procedures remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1–4. The added deep-model formula documents the existing two-layer backbone.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Cora, Citeseer, Photo, ogbn-arxiv, ogbn-products, and ogbn-papers100M with the same unlearning tasks and attack scenarios. The added Cora bounds comparison introduces no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: New Figure 6 adds CGU to the Cora gradient-residual comparison across all three removal scenarios and CEU for edge removal; Figure 2 previously examined ScaleGUN alone. Comparator membership in the utility and attack evaluations is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5 changes the reported linear-utility default from delta = 1e-4 to 1/#edges or 1/#nodes. The stricter edge setting already appeared in v2's appendix. Appendix C.2–C.3 now explicitly retain delta = 1e-4 for several existing experiments; these disclosures do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4 and Figure 6 extend the existing bounds validation to examine comparative tightness and approximation-related residual differences against CGU and CEU. The existing approximation-threshold, noise, batch-size, large-deletion, and attack analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results average five trials with random seeds. The MIA uncertainty entries are unchanged in v2 Table 13 and v3 Table 12; no new statistical reporting procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: V3 Table 1 exactly reproduces v2 Table 12, while the former Table 1 results at delta = 1e-4 disappear. Table 2 replaces utility results under the revised reported privacy setting: ScaleGUN's feature/node total costs change from 42.68/54.85 seconds to 45.29/60.08 seconds. These are not same-setting performance changes. Figure 6 adds comparative residual findings.

T1.justification: The certification definition, assumptions, propagation and unlearning bounds, and formal proofs remain unchanged. Appendix E matches after removing whitespace and pagination differences. The new bounds comparison is empirical evidence, not new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about certified billion-edge graph unlearning, three removal scenarios, and the 20-second random-edge demonstration.

C2.justification: New Appendix C.4 explains ScaleGUN's larger early residual bounds relative to CGU through approximation error, and their later convergence through accumulating unlearning error. It also explains why loose worst-case bounds do not govern retraining. The limitations concerning nonlinear models remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 explicitly describes the deep-model computation and connects its adversarial evaluation to the existing selection procedure. However, it removes v2's rmax = 1e-10 exception accompanying the stricter-privacy edge results now used in Table 1, leaving their relationship to the unchanged Table 7 defaults unclear.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work discussion are unchanged. Additional citations supporting appendix privacy settings reference already cited work and do not revise the research positioning.

P1.justification: V3 adds the conference header and corresponding-author note, makes localized explanatory edits, and inserts Appendix C.4 with subsequent subsection renumbering. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V2 Table 12 is promoted to v3 Table 1, a new three-panel Figure 6 is added, and the existing deep-model figure becomes Figure 7. Nearby tables and text reflow. A new layout defect causes the Figure 6 and Table 11 captions to overlap on page 19.

improvement.justification: The new comparative bounds analysis strengthens evidence about approximation error relative to existing methods, and Table 2 quantifies stricter-privacy node/feature outcomes that v2 only summarized. These modest gains in empirical support and explanation are tempered by the lost experiment-specific rmax disclosure and overlapping captions. The central method and theoretical contribution remain unchanged.
